messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: High error rate (504 / connection-reset) for ACME customer streaming gateway via their dedicated pool (redwood-ded-acme-1). Affected endpoints: /v1/stream/chat, /v1/streams/ws. Triggered at 2026-03-15T02:20:01Z. @Sara K is primary oncall.
Sara K: Acked. pulling logs now. can someone check gateway timeout configs and recent rollout? @Ajay P?
Ajay P: looking. getting a lot of 502/504 from the edge -> pool path. I see a spike in accept failures on the dedicated pool nodes (gRPC: connection reset). Pushing a quick health check to the pool.
Sara K: Client reports intermittent websocket disconnects and long reconnect loops. Customer says their app gateway sees 2-3s TLS handshake stalls then connection reset. Lia, any recent kernel/kernel-tuning changes on that pool?
Lia G: no recent kernel tweaks. there was a model kernel runtime patch yesterday but only applied to hosted and one dedicated shard as canary. checking which shard ACME is on.
Ajay P: ACME is on redwood-ded-acme-1 -> shard-7. Patch not rolled there. logs from shard-7 show repeated accept syscall EPROTO / ECONNRESET around 02:18->02:22Z. copying a sample snippet:
```
[02:19:12.456] gRPC: accept(): errno=104 ECONNRESET from 10.8.32.45:443
[02:19:12.457] http: upstream write failed: short write
[02:19:12.458] worker: kv-cache miss, cold-start
[02:19:14.003] streaming: websocket handshake timeout after 2500ms
```
Sara K: Hmm. Could be a network flakiness between customer app gateway and our edge, or saturation on that shard (thread exhaustion). Quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily route ACME to a hosted fallback pool (no dedicated) 2) increase gateway accept queue/worker threads on shard-7 3) ask customer to bump client-side handshake timeout and exponential backoff. I'd prefer 1 for rapid customer relief. Thoughts?
Customer-ops (ACME): We can accept a routed failover to hosted for 15-30 minutes during business hours. We need minimal disruption to streaming semantics (prefer keepalive).
Ajay P: routing policy exists: can fail ACME traffic to redwood-hosted-streaming-1 as a compatibility fallback. Need approval and then update routing table. Also adjust retry policy to use websocket reconnect jitter and extend handshake timeout.
Matt R: I'm taking secondary oncall for the night. If we plan failover, I'll execute but want to ensure isolation so no co-tenant bleed and cost/accounting flags set.
Sara K: Ok Matt, please prepare failover plan: 1) update routing rule for tenant acme-corp -> hosted fallback 2) set max concurrent streams limit on hosted route to avoid overload 3) enable per-tenant telemetry and alerting 4) communicate to ACME with a bridge link.
Ajay P: prepping routing change now. patch to routing config (short snippet):
```
- tenant: acme-corp
  route: dedicated/redwood-ded-acme-1
+ tenant: acme-corp
  route: hosted/redwood-hosted-streaming-1
  fallback_reason: "streaming accept failures"
  max_conns: 500
```
Applying with canary weight=10% then bump to 100% if healthy.
Sara K: run a canary, monitor for 5 minutes, check client-side reconnection loop telemetry. Lia, can you watch shard-7 resource metrics and kernel logs for any root cause while we fail traffic?
Lia G: watching. pushing a quick kernel tcp_retransmit timeout increase on shard-7 acceptor (temporary) and will roll back if no effect.
Customer-ops (ACME): spinning up a parallel test against the hosted fallback now. will report success/failure in ~2m.
incident-bot: Action: routing change queued by Ajay P. Canary 10% -> started at 02:26:10Z. Pager watchers: Sara K, Matt R.
Ajay P: Canary is green so far (2m). no increase in errors on hosted. client handshake latency on hosted ~120ms vs 2s previously. bumping to 100% now.
Matt R: Failover executed at 02:28:42Z. monitoring...
Sara K: Customer reports restored connection stability and much lower reconnects. Marking mitigated for ACME. keep monitoring for 30m before close.
Lia G: kernel-level logs on shard-7 show a burst of accept queue overflows around 02:18-02:22; unclear if caused by upstream SYN flood or internal thundering herd. dumping pcap for infra team.
Ajay P: I'll open a follow-up to investigate dedicated pool acceptor scaling and add a hard limit on per-tenant concurrent streams to prevent future noisy neighbors.
Customer-ops (ACME): Confirming app behavior improved. We'll keep in hosted fallback for the next hour while we test client backoff changes. thanks all.
Sara K: Handoff: Matt R will own post-mitigation monitoring and action items with assignees: Ajay (routing policy + postmortem), Lia (kernel/acceptor analysis), Sara (customer comms + RCA). Matt — any objections?
Matt R: all good. I'll also add a temporary alert: if dedicated shard-7 error rate >1% within 15m, auto-trigger failover playbook and page oncall.
incident-bot: Incident milestone: Mitigated at 02:28:42Z; postmortem required. Labels: customer-impact, dedicated-pool, websocket, routing-failover.
Sara K: closing notes: customer impact window ~02:18-02:28Z, streaming reconnects and service degradation. No data exfiltration. follow-up RFC for tenant isolation and per-pool backpressure controls is required.
Matt R: will pick up the async postmortem doc and assign owners. thanks team :thumbsup:
